title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes-9
content:
Summary:
Quick personal scramble notes capturing commands tried, error snippets, artifact versions, and hypotheses after the canary failure for release v3.2.1-rc4. Intended to be a single-source breadcrumb log for handoff to SRE/release team and future postmortem.

Context / impact:
- Canary deployment for api-server:v3.2.1-rc4 started at ~2025-02-18T09:32Z in us-west1. 5% traffic shard.
- Symptoms: steady 502s from canary instances, 30-40% p50/p95 latency spike for canary only, slow startup logs showing repeated healthcheck failures. Production (stable) unaffected.
- Canary autoscale triggered and then unhealthy pods evicted; we halted rollout and attempted rollback.

Timeline (local notes):
- 2025-02-18T09:32Z: helm upgrade --install canary (5% traffic)
- 2025-02-18T09:36Z: Observed increase in 502s on canary route (Grafana alert fired)
- 2025-02-18T09:39Z: k get pods -n production --selector=app=api-server,canary=true -> OOMKilled / CrashLoopBackOff observed
- 2025-02-18T09:45Z: Attempted env rollback to prior config (failed to fix)
- 2025-02-18T09:52Z: Performed helm rollback to last stable release on canary subset
- 2025-02-18T10:05Z: Canary still returning 502s; decided to roll entire release back to v3.2.0 stable
- 2025-02-18T10:15Z: Full rollback executed; metrics returned to baseline by ~10:28Z

Commands tried (with relevant output snippets):
- kubectl describe pod api-server-canary-7f8c9 
  -> Events: Back-off restarting failed container; Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 502

- kubectl logs api-server-canary-7f8c9 -c api | tail -n 60\  
  -> 2025-02-18T09:35:12Z ERROR [startup] failed to start http server: dial tcp 10.4.2.15:5432: connect: connection refused
  -> repeated DB connection timeouts, but stable cluster DB reported no issues (checked separately)

- helm history redwood-api --namespace production | tail -n 5\  
  -> REV 42  v3.2.0  deployed 2025-01-24
  -> REV 43  v3.2.1-rc4  deployed 2025-02-18  (canary)

- kubectl exec -it api-server-canary-7f8c9 -c api -- /bin/sh -c 'env | grep REDWOOD_'\  
  -> REDWOOD_DB_HOST=redwood-postgres.cluster.internal
  -> REDWOOD_DB_PORT=5432
  -> REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS=feature_x,experimental_y
  -> NOTE: compared to stable pods — feature flag set was different (stable did NOT have experimental_y)

- docker image inspect registry.redwood.com/api-server:v3.2.1-rc4 --format '{{.Config.Env}}'\  
  -> showed a config.env baked into image with REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS having experimental_y (possible build-time discrepancy)

- curl -v http://canary-route.internal/health
  -> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

- gcloud builds list --filter="images:api-server:v3.2.1-rc4" --limit=5
  -> Build 5623 (success) -> triggered by PR #1423

- git rev-parse --short HEAD (from build logs) -> 3a9f2c4
  -> PR #1423 merged commit 3a9f2c4 changed feature flag logic and added DB connection retry logic removed from stable path

Initial observations / breadcrumbs:
- Canary pods show DB connection refused during startup. However, DB cluster metrics show normal connections. Potential transient network issue between canary nodes and DB (but why only canary?).
- env comparison showed experimental feature flag active only in canary image (either image baked with different ENV or helm chart templating added it).
- Build for v3.2.1-rc4 was triggered by PR #1423 which modified startup path (refs to retry logic and a new dependency on an in-cluster sidecar for caching). PR included a new init container for cache-warm, which may be stalling readiness checks.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Build-time environment/config mismatch: image was built with REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS=experimental_y which toggles a code path that requires cache-init service; cache init not ready -> app fails DB connections (observed).
2) Init container / sidecar ordering bug: new init container introduced in PR causes blocking when cache cluster unavailable; probe times out causing readiness failures and later apparent DB errors.
3) Resource limits wrong: rc4 image heavier, default memory limit triggers OOM during startup under burst - note some pods OOMKilled.
4) Networking/CNI flake: canary nodes scheduled on a subset of hosts with a transient CNI regression; less likely because init container changes align with timing.

Things I tried (and why):
- Helm rollback of canary to previous chart (did not change image) -> no improvement, so chart templating likely not sole cause.
- Full release rollback to v3.2.0 (image rollback) -> resolved issue, points to image-level regression.
- Pulled image locally and started container with env overrides to reproduce start-up locally (quick smoke) -> observed same startup failure when REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS included experimental_y.
- Temporarily toggled REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS to remove experimental_y via helm-set on a canary pod -> pod became healthy (small test, 1 pod), which strongly implicates feature flag path.

Artifact versions / identifiers captured:
- image: registry.redwood.com/api-server:v3.2.1-rc4
- commit: 3a9f2c4 (PR #1423)
- build: gcb-5623 (https://ci.redwood.com/job/release/5623)
- helm chart: redwood-api-chart v1.7.3
- prior stable image: registry.redwood.com/api-server:v3.2.0

Rollback steps executed (what worked):
- helm rollback redwood-api 42 --namespace production (rollback images and chart)
- kubectl rollout status deployment/api-server -n production -> monitored until ready
- Verified traffic using canary routing -> 0% traffic to rc4, baseline latency restored

Immediate next steps / follow-ups (for postmortem and fix):
- Reproduce locally with the exact build environment (I'm storing the gcb logs and dockerfile) to confirm feature flag gating is the cause.
- Add a CI smoke test that boots container with REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS=experimental_y and runs readiness probe script for 30s (catch startup regressions).
- Investigate PR #1423 changes to init container ordering — add explicit readiness gating for cache-warm rather than relying on init container ordering assumptions.
- Remove bake-time feature flags from image; prefer runtime flags from helm/values (prevents build-time mismatch).
- Add a canary preflight step in release pipeline to run a small in-cluster smoke test before shifting traffic (run container in isolated namespace with health checks).

Notes to handoff:
- Handoff to SRE: check if nodes with canary pods had different kernel/CNI versions during 09:32-09:50Z (I did a quick check and didn't find anomalies, but please re-verify).
- Handoff to Release Eng: ask PR author to rework feature flag approach and verify init container semantics.

Linked artifacts / references:
- Jira: INC-2025
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-server/pull/1423
- CI build: https://ci.redwood.com/job/release/5623
- Helm chart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/tree/main/redwood-api-chart
- Confluence (postmortem draft link placeholder): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/12345/Canary+failure+2025-02-18

Quick raw log snippets (for copy/paste):
- ERROR 2025-02-18T09:35:12Z startup failed: dial tcp 10.4.2.15:5432: connect: connection refused
- Healthcheck response: {"status":"unhealthy","checks":{"db":"failed","cache":"init_pending"}}

Personal todo (short):
- [ ] capture exact docker build args from GCB 5623
- [ ] reproduce image locally with REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS toggled
- [ ] open follow-up PR to move experimental_y to runtime flag
- [ ] add CI smoke test and gate in release workflow

Status: DRAFT — will flesh out timeline and attach logs before sending to broader group.

-- Maya
